content:
Numbers up to 100 is the chapter Class 1 Olympiad papers lean on hardest — place value, ordering and skip counting show up in almost every set. Here is what it really tests, the facts a six-year-old needs at their fingertips, the slips that cost easy marks, and a free 10-question test to try right now.

What the Class 1 Numbers 0–100 Olympiad tests

  • Counting forward and backward, and finding the number just before, just after, or between two numbers
  • Place value — reading a two-digit number as so many tens and so many ones
  • Comparing and ordering with the <, > and = signs, and ascending / descending order
  • Skip counting by 2s, 5s and 10s, and telling odd from even

Key facts your child should know

  • A two-digit number is tens + ones: 65 is 6 tens and 5 ones, or 60 + 5.
  • To compare, look at the tens first; only if the tens match do you check the ones. So 86 > 68.
  • Skip counting by 2 gives even numbers; by 5 the number ends in 5 or 0; by 10 it ends in 0.
  • Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8; odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Reading 56 and 65 as the same number — the order of the digits changes the value.
  • When asked for "the 3rd number after 48", counting 48 itself as the first. Start counting from 49.
  • Comparing the ones digit before the tens (thinking 68 > 86 because 8 > 6).

quiz.title: IMO Class 1 Numbers 0–100 Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: In the number 57, what does the digit 7 stand for?
questions.explanation: In 57, the 7 is in the ones place, so its value is just 7.

questions.q: How many even numbers are there between 11 and 21 (not counting 11 and 21)?
questions.explanation: The even numbers between 11 and 21 are 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. That is 5 numbers.

questions.q: How do you write 64 in words?
questions.explanation: 64 has 6 tens and 4 ones, so its name is sixty-four.

questions.q: Veer writes 45, ___, 47. Which number is missing?
questions.explanation: Counting up, after 45 comes 46, and then 47. So the number between them is 46.

questions.q: Veer wrote 75, 70, ___, 60. Which number is missing?
Veer is looking for the number with 3 in the tens place. From 43, 73, 37, 93, which should he choose?
questions.explanation: In 37, the digit 3 sits in the tens place. In the others it does not.

questions.q: Start at 74 and count forward 8 steps. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: Counting on from 74: 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 82. So we reach 82.
Forty-seven means 4 tens and 7 ones, so it is 47.

questions.q: Riya picks the smallest number from 82, 28, 88, 80. Which one does she pick?
questions.explanation: Compare the tens first, then the ones: 28 is the smallest of the four.

faq.q: What does place value mean in Class 1?
faq.a: It means where a digit sits decides its value. In 65 the 6 is in the tens place (worth 60) and the 5 is in the ones place (worth 5).

faq.q: How do I compare two two-digit numbers?
faq.a: Compare the tens digits first. The number with more tens is bigger. If the tens are equal, the bigger ones digit wins.
